decisions.reason: As a core sensor module with its own product page across multiple years and an explicit launch commitment, it fits the firm’s platform strategy and management is likely to persist by treating any weaker uptake as temporary.

Because this is a next-generation replacement of an existing voltage measurement module, the firm has already embedded investment and responsibility in it and is likely to continue supporting it as part of the modular hardware line.

The MQTT proxy disappeared from the website after its launch year, suggesting limited traction and a lower visible commitment than for hardware modules, making it easier to discontinue despite the general tendency to persist.
A CAN bus interface is well aligned with German industrial and embedded use cases, and its continued website presence indicates enough commitment for management to stay the course.
The carbon dioxide sensor module remained visibly marketed over multiple years and supports the firm’s stated expansion of sensing modules, so escalation of commitment favors retaining it.
The touch panel accessory vanished from the website after 2018 and is less central to the announced direction than sensor, interface, or upgraded core modules, so management is more likely to cut it.
